method: For each site: agent status + conversation_targets (baseline), then create_conversation (opens/binds a Studio-owned tab and runs readiness/auth-wall detection), then get_conversation to read readiness, then finish_conversation with closeTab:true for any tab opened here that held no turns. submit_conversation_turn was never called. No account identifiers, emails, or conversation text were captured or stored in this file.

preexistingState.note: A pre-existing claude target (thread claude-chat:c1dcb1ca-...) was already bound with content before this run. It was not touched, not read, and not closed.

Found via list_conversations by targetId after the error; get_conversation confirmed readiness.ready=true, reason=null (composer found, no auth-wall selector matched). Tab closed via finish_conversation(closeTab:true); no turns held.

create_conversation returned state=blocked, readiness.reason='AUTH_WALL' in 4.67s. The owner reports being signed in to Qwen in this browser, so this is suspected to be a false signed-out detection, not a real auth wall.

rootCauseAnalysis.summary: Qwen is the only one of the four create_conversation-eligible sites that reported AUTH_WALL. The short-circuit introduced by the commit the owner flagged (aae7270) makes any requiresAuth:true site with a matching authWallSelector report blocked, even when a usable composer is present.
codePath: src/capture/actions.mjs:941 — `if (requiresAuth === true && hits.length) return { blocked: true, reason: 'auth wall selector matched, sign-in required: ' + hits.slice(0,3).join(', ') }` runs BEFORE the composerUsable check at line 942. For a requiresAuth site, a single matching authWallSelector unconditionally blocks the conversation regardless of whether the composer is actually present and enabled (i.e. regardless of real sign-in state).

src/capture/conversation-browser-adapter.mjs:240 and :260 — `if (auth.blocked) return blocked('AUTH_WALL')` collapses the detailed `auth.reason` string (which names the exact matched selector(s), e.g. 'auth wall selector matched, sign-in required: button.header-right-auth-button') down to the bare code 'AUTH_WALL' before it reaches get_conversation/conversation_capsule. This is a second, independent gap: even when the detection is correct, the operator-visible API loses the diagnostic detail needed to confirm which selector fired.

likelySelector.why: This is the first selector in qwen.mjs's authWallSelectors list, and its own in-file comment (line 48-49) already warns: "Both 'Log in' and 'Sign up' are buttons with this class, not links. A guest composer can still be visible; its presence is not sign-in proof." The comment was written from a logged-OUT capture, so this selector was never validated against a logged-IN Qwen page. If chat.qwen.ai reuses the `header-right-auth-button` class for any other header control once signed in (e.g. an upgrade/account-menu entry point, or the class simply stays in the DOM but hidden only via CSS state the `vis()` visibility check in actions.mjs does not treat as hidden), the selector keeps matching after sign-in and permanently blocks the site.
likelySelector.whyNotConfirmed: Neither get_conversation nor conversation_capsule surfaces the matched-selector list (see codePath above), and no Studio log file recorded the raw detectAuthWall() output for this run (checked always-on.log — no qwen entries; no per-session capture directory was created for qwen because capture never started on a blocked conversation). Confirming the exact selector would require either (a) restoring the dropped auth.reason detail to an operator-visible field, or (b) a live DOM inspection of the signed-in chat.qwen.ai page, both out of scope for this read-only receipt (no source edits, no raw CDP).

recommendedFixNotApplied: Preserve detectAuthWall's full `reason` string (with matched selector names) through conversation-browser-adapter.mjs's blocked() call into an evidence/diagnostic field the operator can read via get_conversation, instead of collapsing it to the bare 'AUTH_WALL' code.

For requiresAuth sites, let composerUsable evidence override a matched authWallSelector when the matched selector is broad/reused (header-right-auth-button) rather than letting selector presence unconditionally win over a usable composer — i.e. reorder/soften the aae7270 priority so a verified usable composer is not discarded by a single ambiguous selector hit.
Re-measure qwen.mjs's authWallSelectors against a confirmed signed-in chat.qwen.ai session and drop or scope button.header-right-auth-button if it is present post-login.

friction: No selector-level diagnostic reaches get_conversation/conversation_capsule; reason is truncated to the code 'AUTH_WALL'.

results.notes: create_conversation's own input schema restricts `site` to the enum [chatgpt, claude, zai, qwen]. Calling it with site=deepseek returned INVALID_CREATE (HTTP 400) in 1.59s before any tab was opened — no cleanup needed. conversation_targets independently shows the pre-existing deepseek target as identity.state='unbound', reason='SITE_UNSUPPORTED', consistent with deepseek not yet having create/bind support in this Studio build. This is a harness capability gap, not a provider sign-in result; readiness for deepseek is NOT_TESTED, not signed-out.
friction: create_conversation tool does not support deepseek; no readiness/auth-wall check could be run through the sanctioned native-tool path.
